question: A 29-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 10 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a prenatal visit. Over the past two weeks, she has felt nauseous in the morning and has had vulvar pruritus and dysuria that started 5 days ago. Her first child was delivered by lower segment transverse cesarean section because of macrosomia from gestational diabetes. Her gestational diabetes resolved after the child was born. She appears well. Ultrasound confirms fetal heart tones and an intrauterine pregnancy. Speculum exam shows a whitish chunky discharge. Her vaginal pH is 4.2. A wet mount is performed and microscopic examination is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Candida albicans infection -> vulvar pruritus and dysuria -> whitish chunky discharge -> vaginal pH 4.2 -> Candida species confirmed on wet mount -> Oral fluconazole -> 85%
CHAIN: Candida albicans infection -> vulvar pruritus and dysuria -> whitish chunky discharge -> vaginal pH 4.2 -> Candida species confirmed on wet mount -> Intravaginal clotrimazole -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient likely has a Candida albicans infection based on symptoms of vulvar pruritus, dysuria, whitish discharge, and low vaginal pH. The wet mount confirming Candida species supports this diagnosis. The most appropriate treatment would be oral fluconazole or intravaginal clotrimazole, both with high efficacy rates for Candida infections.
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including vulvar pruritus, dysuria, whitish discharge, and low vaginal pH, along with the wet mount confirming Candida species, strongly suggest a Candida albicans infection. The most appropriate treatment for this condition is oral fluconazole or intravaginal clotrimazole, both of which have high efficacy rates for Candida infections.
